---
title: "AI Use Log"
---

This log records the substantive ways I used AI while building this portfolio, following the template in Section 3.3 of the Portfolio Guidelines. The tool throughout was Claude (Anthropic), used in two ways: Claude chats inside a project that held the course notes, slides and tutorial sheets, and Claude Code inside VS Code for changes to the files in my repository. I have kept the conversations behind each entry and can talk through any of them in the oral.

I used Claude as an assistant. The ideas, the questions each project asks, the choice of data and models, and every decision about how to compare them were my own. I ran all the R code in my own session, checked every number in my write-ups against my own printed output, and made the final call on anything that went into the portfolio. Claude explained concepts when I got stuck, assisted me with the code and helped me debug it, and pointed out errors and claims that my output did not support. For each write-up I did the analysis first and then discussed the output with Claude. The write-up was built from my own interpretation of that output, Claude helped me refine the writing and fix grammar, and I edited every paragraph into its final wording myself.

## 1. Learning support for Section 1

**Date:** 12 August to 23 September 2026

**Tool used:** Claude (chat)

**What I asked it to help with:** I used Claude as a tutor while working through Section 1. I asked it to explain the three cross-validation strategies (walk-forward, expanding window, sliding window), because I could not see how you validate a forecast without it being circular. I also used it while doing the T-bill ARMA and GARCH lab and the Black Monday exercise, and when I taught myself spectral analysis from Chapter 8 of the notes, since that topic was not covered in lectures. My pattern was to attempt each question first and then ask Claude to explain the concept or check my answer.

**Link to the conversation:** [Time series learning and tutoring](https://claude.ai/chat/756dd3bc-5c7e-4705-aa99-117b2fe95e12)

**What I checked or changed myself:** I checked the explanations against the definitions in the course notes and Salau's guide. For cross-validation I worked through a small numerical example and restated the whole workflow back in my own words before I used it in a journal entry. On the spectral tutorial I worked through each question myself, and one of my answers was corrected (the alias of a frequency of 0.70 is 0.30, a period of about 3.33, not exactly 3), which I then checked against the notes. 

## 2. Practical 1 and setting up the portfolio site

**Date:** 17 August to 30 September 2026

**Tool used:** Claude (chat), Claude Code

**What I asked it to help with:** I asked Claude to help me replicate the `ts()` practical from the slides and then apply the same steps to AAPL data, including debugging an "implicit gaps" error that `ACF()` threw on my tsibble. I then used Claude to plan the layout of the portfolio as a Quarto website following the structure in the guidelines, and used Claude Code to carry out that plan in my repository.

**Link to the conversation:** [Portfolio structure](https://claude.ai/chat/41f568c8-0bf9-4542-8174-3432cd73a06c)

**What I checked or changed myself:** I ran all the practical code myself and only kept the fix for the gaps error (indexing by trading day instead of calendar date) once I understood why tsibble treats weekends as missing values. For the site set-up I wrote the rules Claude Code had to follow: back up the whole folder first, change nothing in the body of my existing files, and list every original file with where it ended up. I checked its plan before approving it, checked the backup and the file-by-file list afterwards, and rendered the site myself.

## 3. Project 1: ARIMA on AAPL

**Date:** September 2026 (first build), 24 October 2026 (review)

**Tool used:** Claude (chat), Claude Code

**What I asked it to help with:** In the first build I chose the question, the data window and the train and test split, and Claude assisted me with the code for the rolling-origin cross-validation and multi-horizon forecasting functions and helped me debug it as I ran it on my data. After Birgit's feedback I used Claude to help me refine the whole project section by section: adding the missing Introduction and exploratory analysis, a forecast plot with prediction intervals, and pointing out any claim in my old write-up that did not match my printed output and function files.

**Link to the conversation:** [Project 1 edit](https://claude.ai/chat/4c5a2e22-115b-42f1-84d2-05ad9053fd09)

**What I checked or changed myself:** While checking the forecast results I found a one-day offset in `forecast_functions.R` that meant the price and returns branches were being scored on different test days, and I fixed it. The review also picked up several explanations from my earlier write-up that my output did not support, including the "geometric compounding" reason for the returns branch winning (the real difference is the drift) and a claim that cross-validation reproduced the AICc ranking. I made the modelling decisions: keeping ARIMA(0,0,0) for returns over AR(1), stating the missing drift model as a limitation rather than fitting it.

## 4. Project 2: GARCH on AAPL

**Date:** September 2026 (first build), 25 October 2026 (review)

**Tool used:** Claude (chat), Claude Code

**What I asked it to help with:** I followed the ten-step workflow in Salau's ARCH and GARCH guide and Claude assisted me with the code for each step using `rugarch` and `FinTS` and helped me debug it, while I checked each step against the guide. In the review I went through every section again with Claude helping me refine the writing, checking each number against my rendered output and fixing duplicate headings, tables that did not render and a heading that broke the table of contents.

**Link to the conversation:** [Project 2 edit](https://claude.ai/chat/88e236da-86ff-42d1-a423-4959dba86e70)

**What I checked or changed myself:** Claude pointed out a backwards reading of the ARCH(1) alpha parameter and two claims that were not supported by my results, and I corrected them. I set a rule for the rest of the portfolio that any edit to my writing had to show the old wording, the new wording and the reason, so I could judge each suggestion myself. I decided not to add a separate Conclusion section, since the Discussion and the one-page summary already do that job, and I confirmed where the 12 lags in the ARCH LM test came from. 

## 5. Project 3: exponential smoothing vs regression on Eskom

**Date:** October 2026 (build), 26 October 2026 (review)

**Tool used:** Claude (chat)

**What I asked it to help with:** I requested the Eskom hourly demand data from the Eskom Data Portal and decided to model daily peak demand. I worked through the report headers strictly in order and wrote the code one chunk at a time, asking Claude to explain methods and to help me debug errors. Once the code was finished I wrote out my interpretation of each result, and Claude helped me refine my wording, fix grammar and point out anything my output did not support.

**Link to the conversation:** [Project 3 edit](https://claude.ai/chat/65c473ea-52b1-49ba-84cb-509d0b2da464)

**What I checked or changed myself:** I chose the data, the models and the comparison design, including the 24 December to 2 January window, which I picked from the festive calendar rather than from the data. Every score in the write-up is given to two decimal places exactly as it printed. Claude pointed out a claim that Easter falls in April every year, which is wrong because Good Friday 2024 was in March, and helped me debug a duplicated plot in the Forecast and Report section. I decided to keep the caveat that I did not test the significance of the comparison with Eskom's own forecast.
